newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela sets 30 bln bolivar TEM auction Wed.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela sets 30 bln bolivar TEM auction Wed.

text.p: The Central Bank of Venezuela announced for Wednesday morning a 20 billion bolivar ($43 million) auction of 180-day "monetary stabilization," or TEM, bills with a 21.99 percent coupon.
The bank said it would also offer five billion bolivars ($11 million) in 269-day bills with a 22.58 percent coupon, and another five billion bolivars of 358-day bills with a 23.19 percent coupon.
No TEMs are due to mature this week.

Coupons are largely unchanged from last week's 25 billion bolivar issue, when 180-, 269- and 359-day notes carried 21.99, 22.57 and 23.19 coupons respectively for effective yields of 22.00, 25.08 and 25.25 percent.
The weekly TEM bill auctions are the Central Bank's principal tool of monetary policy, used to restrict liquidity and establish a benchmark for wider interest rates.
